candidate_reference: resume876: two valid no-exporter PGO full20 boots, 10/20 >=90%, worst OTHER thread_futex_same_cpu Linux_RT/candidate=56.861%
effect: Read-only source audit did not identify a semantics-preserving transaction-level edit capable of closing the 14875ns-to-9397ns same-CPU futex gap. Wake uses a Lazy request consumed at user return; same-CPU notification already avoids IPI. The apparent duplicate Fair virtual-time updates surround enqueue_task, which changes run-queue state, so equivalence of deleting either update was not established. Prior 78.37% full-PGO evidence was from different source/frequency and cannot be compared as a current 816MHz optimization gain. Resume862 already bounded target off-rq activation at >=97.645%, so another generic on/off-rq classification is not the next discriminating test.
decision: No production code edit and no performance claim. Do not implement the subagent's proposed deletion or repeat generic wake-stage probes. A new candidate must identify a changed mechanism and be measured against same-source 816MHz full20, including the other nine failing rows and tail gates.
subagent_limitations: The subagent did not verify every trap return frame or establish a Linux lock-count equivalence; its claim that the two Fair V updates are redundant is not accepted because enqueue lies between them.
